newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma detains Khun Sa aides for having fake notes.
newsitem.headline: Burma detains Khun Sa aides for having fake notes.

text.p: Burmese authorities have arrested three close associates of retired drug baron Khun Sa after they were found with fake 20-kyat bank notes in their possession, Thai army sources said here on Tuesday.

They told Reuters that Burmese soldiers had raided a house in Ho Mong in the northeastern Shan state stronghold of former opium warlord Khun Sa, where they confiscated the fake Burmese bank notes and arrested the three.
"They arrested Chao Suwan, the wife of Kyaw Min and another unidentified man," one army officer said.
Chao Suwan was close to Khun Sa when he was in Ho Mong, and Kyaw Min was his personal doctor.
The Burmese soldiers claimed the fake bank notes were printed in Thailand and were on their way to Rangoon.
Khun Sa, who used to control opium trade in Shan state in the Golden Triangle region where Thailand, Burma and Laos meet, surrendered to Burmese troops last year and now lives in Rangoon.
He is wanted in the United States to face drug charges but Burma has refused to extradite him, saying it will deal with him in its own way.
Khun Sa is said to be running a business empire including transport and hotel businesses in Burma.
